bw: Child struggling to breathe, warm red limbs
w: Albuterol treats bronchospasm alone and does not reverse anaphylactic shock.
Cricothyroidotomy is a last resort if the airway cannot be secured after epinephrine.
p: Anaphylaxis (hypotension, hypoxia, flushing) needs immediate IM epinephrine; antihistamines and steroids are adjuncts.

bw: Knee arthroplasty wound with yellow-green discharge
w: Nafcillin alone cannot control necrotic infected tissue.
Antiseptic dressings do not remove devitalized tissue.
p: Necrotizing or deep wound infection needs prompt debridement plus antibiotics; implant removal is considered if infection involves the prosthesis.

x: keyed answer is a medical note (not a medical concept)

w: Symmetry favors a benign nevus; melanoma is asymmetric.
Smooth, regular borders suggest a benign lesion; melanoma has irregular borders.
p: ABCDE of melanoma: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variegation, Diameter above 6 mm, Evolution.

bw: Gas and cramps after milk or cheese
w: A technetium scan is used for Meckel diverticulum or GI bleeding, not lactose intolerance.
Abdominal ultrasound is normal in lactose intolerance.
p: Lactose intolerance: unabsorbed lactose is fermented by colonic bacteria, raising breath hydrogen; stools have low pH.

bw: Hypopigmented skin lesion with reduced sensation
w: Topical betamethasone would not treat mycobacterial infection.
Amphotericin treats systemic fungal disease, not leprosy.
p: Leprosy (Mycobacterium leprae) causes hypopigmented anesthetic plaques and neuropathy; treat with dapsone plus rifampin (add clofazimine in lepromatous disease).

bw: Back pain, leg weakness, urinary incontinence
w: Bence Jones protein appears in myeloma, which causes lytic lesions.
A thyroid enlargement would not explain sclerotic metastases.
p: Prostate cancer metastasizes to bone with osteoblastic (sclerotic) lesions and can cause cord compression, an oncologic emergency.

bw: Scrotal pain, dysuria, positive Prehn sign
Increased testicular blood flow on Doppler
w: Metronidazole does not cover Neisseria or Chlamydia.
Surgical exploration is for testicular torsion, which has reduced flow.
p: Epididymitis in sexually active men under 35 is usually gonococcal or chlamydial: ceftriaxone plus doxycycline; Prehn sign is relief with elevation.

w: Colon adenocarcinoma is not specifically linked to HIV.
Thymoma is associated with myasthenia gravis, not AIDS.
p: Kaposi sarcoma (HHV-8) is AIDS-defining along with non-Hodgkin lymphoma and cervical cancer.

bw: Continuous motor unit activity on EMG
w: Anti-Hu causes sensory neuronopathy and encephalomyelitis in small cell lung cancer.
Anti-Ri causes opsoclonus-myoclonus.
p: Stiff-person syndrome: axial rigidity with spasms; paraneoplastic forms (lung, breast) have anti-amphiphysin, otherwise anti-GAD.

w: Pseudomonas is linked to puncture wounds through shoes and swimming.
Fusobacterium is an oral anaerobe less typical than Pasteurella in dog bites.
p: Pasteurella multocida is the main bite-wound pathogen (dogs and cats); treat with amoxicillin-clavulanate.

bw: Lateral hip pain, worse lying on that side
w: Iliotibial band syndrome causes lateral knee pain rather than hip pain.
Lumbosacral radiculopathy causes pain below the knee with neurologic signs.
p: Trochanteric bursitis or gluteal tendinopathy: lateral hip tenderness, treated with NSAIDs, physical therapy and injection.

w: Intermittent explosive disorder lacks persistent irritable mood between outbursts and is diagnosed after age 6 with brief outbursts.
Conduct disorder involves violation of others' rights and rules.
p: DMDD: severe recurrent outbursts three or more times weekly with persistently irritable mood, onset before age 10.

w: HbA1c is unreliable for diagnosing gestational diabetes.
The 75 g test is the diagnostic step after a positive screen, not the screen itself.
p: Screen at 24-28 weeks with a nonfasting 1-hour 50 g glucose load; a result at or above 130-140 mg/dL leads to the 3-hour 100 g test.
